query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Earlier studies of other self-lubricating material systems reported low coefficients of friction at 704 °C and favorable friction and wear behavior over broad temperature ranges. However, these results do not resolve the limited understanding of wide-temperature tribological performance in CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys, and effectiveness must be maintained as operating temperature, load, and environment vary. Formulate one hypothesis that identifies a single intervention without presupposing its class, explains its mechanism, predicts friction and wear relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, defines its temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, relates it to prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A trace addition of tungsten (≈0.5 at.%) to a pure CoCrFeNi high entropy alloy will promote an in‐situ, self-adaptive tribolayer that transitions its lubrication mechanism from low-temperature adhesion mitigation to high-temperature protective glazing, thereby maintaining a low coefficient of friction and low wear rate over the full range from room temperature to 800 °C.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic, single-phase CoCrFeNi high entropy alloy prepared without secondary phases.
generation.intervention: Reactive alloying by substituting approximately 0.5 at.% tungsten into the CoCrFeNi matrix during alloy synthesis.
generation.conditions: Dry sliding wear tests under ambient atmosphere, with the temperature ramping from room temperature to 800 °C and under moderate to high normal loads.
generation.structural_mediator: W-induced lattice distortion that favors the localized, reactive segregation of tungsten-rich phases (such as mixed tungsten oxides or intermetallic compounds) at the friction interface.
generation.mechanism: The tungsten atoms, due to their large atomic size and high enthalpy differences with the base elements, increase lattice distortion and serve as nucleation sites for tribo-chemically active phases. At lower temperatures, these sites help inhibit adhesive wear, while at higher temperatures the reactive segregation promotes rapid formation of a protective glaze layer that mitigates oxidative and adhesive wear.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the baseline pure CoCrFeNi alloy, the tungsten-alloyed variant will show a consistently lower friction coefficient and reduced wear volume throughout the temperature span. The formation of a dynamic tribolayer adapting its structure to temperature will be evident in cross-sectional analyses.
generation.baseline: The pure CoCrFeNi alloy, which under sliding conditions exhibits variations in friction and wear performance over the temperature range due to insufficient and non-adaptive tribolayer formation.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is applicable for sliding wear conditions in ambient air over the temperature range from room temperature up to 800 °C and under variable loading conditions typical of industrial or mechanical applications.
generation.uncertainty: While reactive alloying with tungsten has been shown to enhance high-temperature wear resistance in related systems (e.g., AlCoCrFeNiW coatings as per PMC8470387 and adaptive tribolayer formation in Ni-based CCAs as per PMC10241162), its effect when applied to a pure CoCrFeNi matrix remains untested. The exact nature of the tribolayer phase and its stability across the entire temperature range is uncertain; further investigation is needed to verify that the tungsten-induced mechanisms observed in other systems will translate to this matrix.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate two sets of samples: one of the baseline pure CoCrFeNi alloy and one doped with ≈0.5 at.% tungsten. Conduct ball-on-disk sliding experiments over a temperature range from room temperature to 800 °C under identical loads and environmental conditions. Collect in-situ friction data and post-test wear measurements.
measurements: Continuous recording of the friction coefficient during sliding
Wear volume determination via 3D optical profilometry
Microstructural and phase analysis (SEM/EDS and XRD) of wear tracks to verify tribolayer formation and composition
Comparative assessment of the evolution of tribolayer morphology at various temperatures
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis will be falsified if the tungsten-alloyed samples do not exhibit a statistically significant decrease in the friction coefficient and wear rate across the entire temperature range relative to the pure CoCrFeNi samples, or if no adaptive, tungsten-enriched tribolayer is observed under the defined test conditions.
